FOREWORD

0.

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 March 1975, after the draft finalized by the Paints and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 .This standard was first published in 1932 and was largely based on the interim coordinated draft produced with the assistance of the representatives of manufacturers and of various departments and authorities of the Government of India, by the coordinating Subcommittee of the No. 5 Standing Committee on Specifications for Paint and Allied Stores of the General Headquarters, India ( now Army Headquarters ). 0.3 In this revision, which has been prepared based on the recommendations of an Ad hoc Panel specially set up for review of Indian Standards for paints, the requirement for maximum acid value has been modified from 25 to 15. The material according to this revised standard shall be of one type only as against two classes in the earlier version. The test for scratch hardness on `the panels prepared with the material shall be carried out only by a mechanical tester. Amendments No. 1 and 2 to this standard have been incorporated in this revision. 0.4 For the purpose standard is complied the result of a test IS : 2-1960*. The value should be the of deciding whether a particular requirement of this with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing or analysis! shall be rounded off in accordance with number of significant places retained in the rounded off same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS : 337 - 1975 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, 1972* and IS : 197-1969t shall apply. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Description - The material shall be clear, foreign matter, sediment and undissolved water. transparent and free from the definitions given in IS : 6667-

3.2 Composition - The material shall be based on resins, drying oils, driers and thinners in suitable proportions to satisfy the requirement of this standard. 3.3 Resistance 1964: with 24 test. 3.4 The material to Water - When tested as prescribed in 23 of IS : 101hours immersion, the film of the material shall pass the shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1.

d) Month and year of manufacture; and e) Batch No. or lot No. in code or otherwise. 5.1.1 The containers may also be marked with the Standard Mark.

NOTE - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products cmered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that'they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked p'mducts are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard.
